questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The length of the axis of the conic $9 x^2+4 y^2-6 x+4 y+1=0$ are
questions.solution:
Given that equation of conic is $\begin{aligned} & \quad \begin{array}{l} 9 x^2+4 y^2-6 x+4 y+1=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad 9 x^2-6 x+4 y^2+4 y+1=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad 9\left(x-\frac{1}{3}\right)^2+4\left(y+\frac{1}{2}\right)^2=1 \\ \text { or, } \quad \frac{\left(x-\frac{1}{3}\right)^2}{\frac{1}{9}}+\frac{\left(y+\frac{1}{2}\right)^2}{\frac{1}{4}}=1 \end{array} . \end{aligned}$
Comparing it with standard equation of ellipse $\frac{X^2}{a^2}+\frac{Y^2}{b^2}=1$, we get $a=\frac{1}{3}, b=\frac{1}{2}$ Length of major axis $=2 b=2 \times \frac{1}{2}=1$ and length of minor axis $=2 a=2 \times \frac{1}{3}=\frac{2}{3}$

questions.q: The radius of the circle passing through the foci of the ellipse $\frac{x^2}{4}+\frac{4 y^2}{7}=1$ and having its centre at $\left(\frac{1}{2}, 2\right)$ is
questions.solution:
Given equation of ellipse is $\frac{x^2}{4}+\frac{y^2}{\frac{7}{4}}=1$
Here,
$a^2=4$
and
$b^2=\frac{7}{4}\becauseb^2=a^2\left(1-e^2\right)\therefore \quad \frac{7}{4}=4\left(1-e^2\right)\Rightarrow \quad e^2=1-\frac{7}{16}=\frac{9}{16} \Rightarrow e=\frac{3}{4}$,
Thus, the foci are $\left( \pm \frac{3}{2}, 0\right)$.
The radius of the required circle
$\begin{aligned}
& =\sqrt{\left(\frac{3}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\right)^2+(0-2)^2} \\
& =\sqrt{5}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Tangent to the ellipse $\frac{x^2}{32}+\frac{y^2}{18}=1$ having slope $\frac{-3}{4}$ meet the coordinate axis at $A$ and $B$. Then, the area of $\triangle A O B$, where $O$ is the origin, is
questions.solution:
Equation of tangent with the slope $\frac{-3}{4}$ is $y=\frac{-3}{4} x+C$.
According to condition of tangency,
$C=\sqrt{32 \times\left(\frac{-3}{4}\right)^2+18}=\sqrt{18+18}=6\begin{array}{lrl}\therefore & y & =\frac{-3}{4} x+6 \\ \Rightarrow & 4 y+3 x & =24\end{array}$
Since, it meet the coordinate axes in $A$ and $B$.
$\therefore A \equiv(8,0) \text { and } B \equiv(0,6)\therefore$ Required area $=\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 6=24$ sq units

questions.q: The condition for the line $l x+m y+n=0$ to be a normal to $\frac{x^2}{25}+\frac{y^2}{9}=1$ is
questions.solution:
Given equation of line is $l x+m y+n=0$ and equation of ellipse is $\frac{x^2}{25}+\frac{y^2}{9}=1$. $\therefore$ The equation of any normal to the ellipse is $5 x \sec \theta-3 y \operatorname{cosec} \theta=25-9$
$\Rightarrow \quad 5 x \sec \theta-3 y \operatorname{cosec} \theta-16=0$ As the Eq. (i) is the normal to the ellipse. $\therefore \quad \frac{5 \sec \theta}{l}=\frac{-3 \operatorname{cosec} \theta}{m}=\frac{-16}{n}\Rightarrow \quad \cos \theta=\frac{5 n}{-16 l}$ and $\sin \theta=\frac{3 n}{16 m}\because \quad \cos ^2 \theta+\sin ^2 \theta=1\therefore \quad\left(\frac{5 n}{16 l}\right)^2+\left(\frac{3 n}{16 m}\right)^2=1\Rightarrow \quad \frac{25 n^2}{256 l^2}+\frac{9 n^2}{256 m^2}=1\Rightarrow \quad \frac{25}{l^2}+\frac{9}{m^2}=\frac{256}{n^2}$

questions.q: The minimum radius vector of the curve $\frac{a^2}{x^2}+\frac{b^2}{y^2}=1$ is of length
questions.solution:
Given curve is $\frac{a^2}{x^2}+\frac{b^2}{y^2}=1$
Let radius vector is ' $r$ '
$\begin{array}{ll}
\therefore & r^2=x^2+y^2 \\
\Rightarrow r^2 & =\frac{a^2 y^2}{y^2-b^2}+y^2 \quad\left(\because \frac{a^2}{x^2}+\frac{b^2}{y^2}=1\right)
\end{array}
For minimum value of $r$,
$\begin{aligned}
& & \frac{d\left(r^2\right)}{d y} & =0 \\
\Rightarrow & & \frac{-2 y b^2 a^2}{\left(y^2-b^2\right)^2}+2 y & =0 \\
\Rightarrow & & y^2 & =b(a+b) \\
\therefore & & x^2 & =a(a+b) \\
\Rightarrow & & r^2 & =(a+b)^2 \\
\Rightarrow & & r & =a+b
\end{aligned}

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the line $l x+m y+n=0$ cuts the ellipse $\frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{25}=1$ in points whose eccentoric angles differ by $\frac{\pi}{2}$, then $\frac{a^2 l^2+b^2 m^2}{n^2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let the points of intersection of the line and the ellipse be $(a \cos \theta, b \sin \theta)$ and $\left\{a \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}+\theta\right), b \sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}+\theta\right)\right\}$, since they lie on the
given line $\quad l x+m y+n=0$.
$l a \cos \theta+m b \sin \theta+n=0\Rightarrow \quad l a \cos \theta+m b \sin \theta=-n$
and  $l a \sin \theta+m b \cos \theta+n=0l a \sin \theta-m b \cos \theta=n$
squarring and adding, we get,
$a^2 l^2+b^2 m^2=2 n^2 \quad \Rightarrow \frac{a^2 l^2+b^2 m^2}{n^2}=2$.

questions.q: If the tangent to ellipse $x^2+2 y=1$ at point $P\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, \frac{1}{2}\right)$ meets the auxiliary circle at the points $R$ and $Q$, then tangents to circle at $Q$ and $R$ intersect at
questions.solution:
Equation of tangent to ellipse at given point is $x\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)+2 y\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=1$. $\Rightarrow \quad x+\sqrt{2} y=\sqrt{2}$ ....(i)
Now, $Q R$ is chord of contact of circle $x^2+y^2=1$ with respect to point $T(h, K)$. then, $\quad Q R \equiv h x+K y=1$ ....(ii) Equations (i) and (ii) represent same straight line, then comparing ratio of coefficients we have $\frac{h}{1}=\frac{K}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ Hence; $(h, K) \equiv\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, 1\right)$

questions.q: If $P$ is a variable point on the ellipse $\frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$, with $A A^{\prime}$ as major axis. Then, the maximum value of the area of the $\triangle A P A^{\prime}$ is
questions.solution:
The maximum area corresponds to when $P$ is at either end of the minor axis.
$\therefore$ Required area $=\frac{1}{2}(2 a) b=a b$ sq unit

questions.q: Tangent is drawn to ellipse $\frac{x^2}{27}+\frac{y^2}{1}=1$ at $(3 \sqrt{3} \cos \theta, \sin \theta)$, where $\left(\theta \in\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\right)$. Then, the value of $\theta$ such that the sum of intercept on axes made by this tangent is minimum, is
questions.solution:
Equation of tangent is drawn at a $(3 \sqrt{3} \cos \theta, \sin \theta)$ to the curve
$\text { is } \frac{x \cos \theta}{3 \sqrt{3}}+\frac{y \sin \theta}{1}=1$
Thus, sum of intercepts
$\begin{array}{ll} 
& =(3 \sqrt{3} \sec \theta+\operatorname{cosec} \theta)=f(\theta) \quad \text{(say)} \\
\Rightarrow & f^{\prime}(\theta)=3 \sqrt{3} \sec \theta \tan \theta-\operatorname{cosec} \theta \cot \theta \\
& =\frac{3 \sqrt{3} \sin ^3 \theta-\cos ^3 \theta}{\sin ^2 \theta \cos ^2 \theta} \\
\text { Put } & f^{\prime}(\theta)=0 \\
\Rightarrow & \sin ^3 \theta=\frac{1}{3^{3 / 2}} \cos ^3 \theta \\
\Rightarrow & \tan \theta=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\
\Rightarrow & \theta=\frac{\pi}{6}
\end{array}$

questions.q: The equation of the ellipse whose axes are parallel to the coordinate axes having its centre at the point $(2,-3)$ and focus at $(3,-3)$ and one vertex at $(4,-3)$ is
questions.solution:
Let $2 a$ and $2 b$ be the major and minor axes of the ellipse. Then, its equation is $\frac{(x-2)^2}{a^2}+\frac{(y+3)^2}{b^2}=1$..(i)
$\Rightarrow \quad \sqrt{(4-2)^2+(-3+3)^2}=aa=2$...(ii) Here, $C S=a e\Rightarrow \quad \sqrt{(2-3)^2+(-3+3)^2}=a e\Rightarrow \quad a e=1$...(iii) From Eqs. (ii) and (iii), we get $e=\frac{1}{2}$ Now, $b^2=a^2\left(1-e^2\right)\Rightarrow \quad b^2=4\left(1-\frac{1}{4}\right)=3$ On substituting the values of $a$ and $b$ in Eq. (i) we get $\frac{(x-2)^2}{4}+\frac{(y+3)^2}{3}=1$

questions.q: The area of the quadrilateral formed by the tangents at the end point of latusrectum to the ellipse $\frac{x^2}{9}+\frac{y^2}{5}=1$ is
questions.solution:
The quadrilateral formed by the tangents at the end points of the latusrectum is a rhombus. It is symmetrical about the axes.
So, total area is four times the area of the right triangle formed by the tangents and the axes in the first quadrant. Now, $\begin{aligned} & a e=\sqrt{a^2-b^2} \\ & a e=2 \end{aligned}\therefore$ The co-ordinates of one end point latusrectum are $\left(2, \frac{5}{3}\right)$. The equation of tangent at that point is $\frac{x}{\frac{9}{2}}+\frac{y}{3}=1$, this meets the co-ordinate axes at $A\left(0, \frac{9}{2}\right)$ and $B(3,0)$. Area of $\triangle A O B=\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{9}{2} \times 3=\frac{27}{4}$ Hence, the area of rhombus $A B C D=4 \times \frac{27}{4}=27 \text { sq units }$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The locus of the extrimities of the latusrectum of the family of ellipses $b^2 x^2+y^2=a^2 b^2$ having a given major axis, is
questions.solution:
Given equation is
$b^2 x^2+y^2=a^2 b^2\Rightarrow \quad \frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{a^2 b^2}=1$  ....(i)
Above equation of an ellipse with semi-major axis (a) and semi-minor axis (ab).
N̦ow, ecentricity,
$e=1-\frac{a^2 b^2}{a^2} \Rightarrow b^2=1-e^2$  ....(ii)
Let $(x, y)$ be extrimities of latusrectum, then
$\begin{aligned} x & =a e \text { and } y= \pm \frac{a^2 b^2}{a} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{x}{a} & =e \text { and } \frac{y}{a}= \pm b^2\end{aligned}$
From Eq. (ii), we get
$\pm \frac{y}{a}=1-\frac{x^2}{a^2} \Rightarrow \pm a y+x^2=a^2$
Hence, locus of latusrectum is $x^2 \pm a y=a^2$.
